full_judgment:
11. We are to see whether classification of the borrowers of financial institutions together in one group from other borrowers of private individuals and institutions other than financial institutions is on just, fair, reasonable and rational basis or unjust, arbitrary and discriminatory and the classification is sought to achieve the object for which the Act has been passed. In other words whether such classification for the purpose of legislation is permissible Petitioners relied on the decision in the case of State of West Bongo vs. Anwar Ali reported in AIR 1952 SC 75. In that case West Bengal Special Courts Act 1950 authorizing the State Government to transfer any criminal case from ordinary criminal court to a Special Tribunal for speedy trial was declared ultra vires of Article 14 of the Constitution of India on the ground that it ignored the principle of classification followed in the Code of Criminal Procedure and it proceeded to lay down a new procedure without making any attempt to particularize or classify the offences or cases to which it is to apply. 

 13. After the Constitution of Pakistan 1956 came into force provisions of sections 3 and 31 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 providing for compulsory acquisition of rent-receiving interests and payment of compensation at different rates was challenged as violative of the equality provision of Article 5 of the Constitution of Pakistan 1956 in the case or Jibendra Kishore Vs. Province of East Pakistan reported in 9 DLR (SC) 21. The contention was rejected by the Pakistan Supreme Court observing as follows: "Another generalization more frequently stated, is that the guarantee of equal protection of law requires that all persons shall be treated alike under like circumstances and conditions both in the privileges conferred and in the liabilities imposed. In the application of these principles, however it has always been recognized that classification of persons or things is in no way repugnant to the equality doctrine, provided the classification is not arbitrary or capricious, is natural and reasonable and bears a fair and substantial relation to the object of the legislation"
